result:
The proposed answer of 0 is very likely wrong. I did not verify this by direct construction.

The solution's argument rests on checking a few well-known candidates (the Mycielskian of C₇, the Grötzsch graph, the Chvátal graph) and then claiming that "systematic attempts" lead to contradictions. That is not a proof that no such graph exists. The Chvátal graph, for instance, is dismissed without any actual check for an induced C₇ or an induced P₇.

The problem asks "how many" such graphs exist, which suggests a small positive finite number. I also recall a published classification of 4-vertex-critical (P₇, C₃)-free graphs that includes some containing an induced C₇. I am recalling this from memory and cannot confirm the exact count here.

VERDICT: REJECT
